layers.title: Chandrayaan-2 TMC-2 DTM hillshade (100 m, derived)
layers.caption: From TMC-2 DTM ch2_tmc_ndn_20211115T1549013919 (10 m), block-averaged to 100 m, hillshade az 315°/alt 30°. Strip spans 87.5°S–59.9°S; it does NOT cover Shiv Shakti, so a horizon there still relies on LOLA (LDEM_60S_240M here; LDEM_64S/SLDEM2015 would be finer).

layers.title: Chandrayaan-2 DFSAR L-band cross-pol ratio (100 m, derived; NOT CPR)
layers.caption: Cross-pol ratio 10·log10(2⟨|HV|,|VH|⟩/(HH+VV)) from ch2_sar_ncxl_20260308t062017233 (L-band full-pol, ~84.2°S 33.4°E). This is NOT the circular polarisation ratio (CPR needs complex SLI phase) and is not an ice detection. σ0 calibration constant (K = 70.31 dB, assumed DN²/10^(K/10)) is UNVERIFIED. Median −7.9 dB (p5–p95 −13.2 to −5.2 dB).

layers.title: Chandrayaan-2 OHRC preview around Shiv Shakti (2 m, PRE-LANDING)
layers.caption: OHRC image ch2_ohr_ncp_20230506T0548584558, acquired 2023-05-06, BEFORE the August 2023 landing: the lander is not visible and no lander pin is drawn. ~2.6 × 2.7 km, north up, centred on the published landing coordinates; absolute position may be off by kilometres (SPICE-limited georeferencing, arXiv:2602.14993).

layers.title: Chandrayaan-3 ChaSTE temperatures (archive, 30-min means)
layers.caption: Archive-calibrated values, NOT corrected for the probe-induced perturbations applied in Durga Prasad et al. 2025 (archive max ≈353 K vs the paper's 355 K). S2 is plotted as the near-surface sensor (as in the paper), not S1. The early span includes commissioning data.
